title: No Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint - Brute Force Attack Possible
description: The login endpoint at /login does not implement rate limiting, account lockout mechanisms, or throttling controls. An attacker can perform unlimited login attempts without any delays, temporary blocking, or account suspension. Each failed login attempt returns an HTTP 200 status code immediately, allowing continuous brute force attacks without any resistance from the application. The application accepts all authentication attempts at high frequency (8-25ms per request) with no delay progression or blocking mechanisms.
impact: An attacker can conduct unlimited brute force attacks against user accounts without encountering any delays or temporary lockouts. Combined with the weak default credentials ('user/user') already present in the system, this creates a critical risk for rapid account enumeration and unauthorized access. An attacker could systematically test thousands of password combinations for each username in a matter of minutes without encountering any resistance. This significantly increases the likelihood of successful account compromise through password guessing, particularly when combined with common password dictionaries or leaked password lists.
evidence:
POC executed successfully demonstrating brute force vulnerability. Script performed 10 rapid sequential login attempts with different passwords:

All 10 attempts returned HTTP 200 status codes:
- Attempt 1: HTTP 200 (10ms)
- Attempt 2: HTTP 200 (9ms)
- Attempt 3: HTTP 200 (9ms)
- Attempt 4: HTTP 200 (8ms)
- Attempt 5: HTTP 200 (8ms)
- Attempt 6: HTTP 200 (8ms)
- Attempt 7: HTTP 200 (9ms)
- Attempt 8: HTTP 200 (9ms)
- Attempt 9: HTTP 200 (25ms)
- Attempt 10: HTTP 200 (9ms)

Results confirmed:
- Total Attempts: 10
- Successful Responses (200/302): 10/10
- Immediate Responses (< 500ms): 10/10
- No rate limiting (HTTP 429) responses received
- No account lockout (HTTP 403) responses received
- No throttling or delays imposed by server

The vulnerability allows unlimited brute force attacks without any throttling or blocking mechanisms.
remediation:
1. Implement rate limiting on the login endpoint using Flask-Limiter or similar library - limit to 5 login attempts per minute per IP address or username.
2. Implement account lockout mechanisms - temporarily lock accounts after 5-10 failed login attempts for 15-30 minutes with notification to the user.
3. Add progressive delays - implement exponential backoff starting after 3 failed attempts (e.g., 1s delay, 2s, 4s, etc.).
4. Implement CAPTCHA verification - require CAPTCHA after 3-5 failed login attempts to prevent automated brute force.
5. Log all failed login attempts with timestamps, IP addresses, and usernames for monitoring and alerting.
6. Implement IP-based rate limiting at the web server level (nginx, Apache) in addition to application-level controls.
7. Monitor for brute force patterns and alert on suspicious activities (multiple failed attempts from same IP or targeting same account).
8. Consider implementing multi-factor authentication (MFA) as an additional layer of protection against account compromise.
references: OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures, CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames, CWE-355: Insufficient Restriction of Interaction Between Mutable Resources and Web Templates, CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
toolCallDescription: Documenting the brute force vulnerability on login endpoint with confirmed POC demonstrating unlimited login attempts without rate limiting
